description: Build the backtest ENGINE + BROKER/position model + METRICS. The broker simulates XAUUSD market buy/sell with SL/TP, partial closes (T1/T2/T3), trailing-stop modification, hedging (both directions open at once, HEDGE account), spread-based fills (buy at ask, sell at bid, SL/TP filled when the quote crosses), commission per lot, and equity/balance/drawdown tracking on every tick. The metrics module produces a dict whose KEYS MATCH tools/analyze_report.py's summary['metrics'] schema so automation/tuner/scoring.py score() consumes it directly. Depends on FEAT-001 (loader/bars/config). STDLIB ONLY, pure ASCII, Python 3.9+. Uses only tiny synthetic tick fixtures in tests with hand-computed expected P&L.
steps: BROKER MODEL python_bt/broker.py: define a Position dataclass (side 'buy'/'sell', volume_lots, entry_price, sl, tp, open_ts, tags e.g. t1_done/t2_done bools, breakeven_done bool, initial_volume). Define a Broker class holding: balance, equity, deposit (from config.INITIAL_DEPOSIT), open positions list (supports MULTIPLE simultaneous, both directions = hedging), closed-trade ledger, and running peak-equity / max-drawdown trackers. Config comes from python_bt/config.py (POINT_SIZE, CONTRACT_SIZE, TICK_SIZE, TICK_VALUE, COMMISSION_PER_LOT_PER_SIDE). P&L for a fill: for buy, profit_price = (exit - entry); for sell, (entry - exit); money = profit_price / TICK_SIZE * TICK_VALUE * volume_lots. Commission charged per lot per side on OPEN and on each CLOSE (partial closes charge on the closed volume). Methods: open(side, volume, price_bid, price_ask, sl, tp, ts) -> fills buy at ask, sell at bid, deducts open commission; on_quote(bid, ask, ts) -> for every open position check SL/TP crossing (buy SL hit when bid<=sl, buy TP when bid>=tp; sell SL when ask>=sl, sell TP when ask<=tp) and close at the stop/target price, updating balance + ledger + commission; close_partial(position, volume, price_bid, price_ask, ts, reason) and close_full(...); modify_sl(position, new_sl) for trailing/breakeven; recompute floating equity = balance + sum(open position unrealized money) on every quote and update peak/trough for drawdown. Keep per-tick work O(open_positions), not O(all_ticks_so_far).

DRAWDOWN + LEDGER: track equity peak and the max money drawdown from peak (maximal_drawdown_money = largest peak-to-trough equity drop; relative_drawdown_money/pct = the drop giving the largest PERCENT relative to the peak at which it started, matching MT5 'relative drawdown' semantics; absolute_drawdown = deposit minus lowest-ever balance-based low). Record each closed deal's realized money (net of commission) into the ledger with side, volumes, entry/exit, ts, so metrics can compute win/loss stats. This ledger is the analog of the MT5 report's per-deal rows.

METRICS python_bt/metrics.py: compute_metrics(ledger, equity_curve, deposit) -> dict using EXACTLY these keys (match reports/samples/sample_report.summary.json): total_net_profit, gross_profit, gross_loss, profit_factor (gross_profit/abs(gross_loss); handle zero-loss), expected_payoff (net/total_trades), recovery_factor (net/maximal_drawdown_money), sharpe_ratio (mean/stdev of per-trade returns via statistics; 0 if <2 trades), absolute_drawdown, maximal_drawdown_money, maximal_drawdown_pct, relative_drawdown_money, relative_drawdown_pct, total_trades (closed positions count; define a 'trade' as one round-trip position open->fully closed, matching how partials roll up so counts are comparable), total_deals, win_rate_pct, largest_profit_trade, largest_loss_trade, average_profit_trade, average_loss_trade, max_consecutive_wins_count, max_consecutive_wins_money, max_consecutive_losses_count, max_consecutive_losses_money. Document in a comment how a 'trade' vs 'deal' is defined here vs MT5 (a partial close is a deal; the round-trip is the trade) since this affects total_trades that score() reads. Ensure relative_drawdown_pct is populated because scoring.py's hard 15% ceiling reads it.

ENGINE python_bt/engine.py: an event loop that drives a Strategy (interface defined in FEAT-003; here define the minimal expected protocol: strategy.on_bar(bar, context) and/or strategy.on_tick(tick, context) returning intents, or a callback-based context object the strategy calls to request open/close/modify). Design: the engine feeds EITHER the tick stream (tick mode, tick-accurate fills) OR M5 bars (fast mode) built from the same ticks; in bar mode the strategy decides on bar close but fills still use the bar's last bid/ask and SL/TP checks still run per-quote where feasible (document the approximation). Provide a Context/Broker-facing API the strategy uses: context.buy(volume, sl, tp), context.sell(...), context.positions, context.close_partial(...), context.modify_sl(...), plus indicator access. The engine: on each tick, call broker.on_quote (to fire SL/TP) then let the strategy act on bar close; track the equity curve; at end return compute_metrics(...) plus a JSON-serializable result dict {metrics: {...}, score: score(metrics), params: {...}, meta: {data range, tick/bar count, mode, config constants used}}. IMPORT score from automation.tuner.scoring (add the tuner dir to sys.path via a small bootstrap consistent with automation/tuner/tests/_bootstrap.py, or import by adjusting sys.path in a helper) - do NOT reimplement scoring.

SCORING WIRE-UP: add a small python_bt/scoring_bridge.py (or inline in engine) that makes automation/tuner/scoring.py importable from python_bt without duplicating it: insert the automation/tuner path on sys.path and `from scoring import score`. Confirm score(metrics_dict) returns the two-tier value and that a >15% relative_drawdown_pct result scores in the lower tier. This proves the Python path and the tuner agree on 'better'.

TESTS python_bt/tests/test_broker.py + test_metrics.py + test_engine.py: TINY synthetic tick fixtures with HAND-COMPUTED expected P&L. Cover: (a) buy fills at ask, sell at bid; commission deducted on open and close; (b) a buy that hits TP closes at TP with the exact money = (tp-entry)/TICK_SIZE*TICK_VALUE*lots minus commission (hand-computed); (c) a buy that hits SL; a sell SL/TP mirror; (d) partial close reduces volume and realizes proportional P&L; a second partial then full close; (e) hedging: a buy AND a sell open simultaneously and both tracked; (f) drawdown: a scripted equity path with a known peak-to-trough gives the expected maximal_drawdown_money/pct and relative_drawdown_pct; (g) metrics: a small ledger with 3 wins / 2 losses gives hand-computed profit_factor, win_rate_pct, expected_payoff, largest/avg win/loss, max consecutive wins/losses; (h) score() integration: build a metrics dict with relative_drawdown_pct 10 vs 20 and assert the 10% one scores strictly higher (tier separation). Engine test: run a 2-3 bar scripted feed with a trivial always-buy stub strategy and assert a trade is opened/closed and metrics+score come back. Never touch the 526MB CSV.

VERIFY: python3 -m py_compile the new modules and tests; python3 -m unittest discover -s python_bt/tests -p 'test_*.py' -q (all green incl. FEAT-001 tests); confirm score() import works from python_bt (a one-liner import check); grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7F]' new files (empty); tools (16) + tuner (38) suites still green; GaganEA.mq5 untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Broker fills buy at ask / sell at bid, charges commission per lot per side on open and close, and closes positions when the quoted side crosses SL/TP at the stop/target price.

Broker supports multiple simultaneous positions including both directions at once (hedging) and supports partial closes that reduce volume and realize proportional P&L, plus SL modification (breakeven/trailing).
Equity/balance/drawdown are tracked per quote; maximal_drawdown_money/pct and relative_drawdown_money/pct are computed with MT5-comparable semantics.

compute_metrics returns a dict whose keys match reports/samples/sample_report.summary.json's metrics schema, including relative_drawdown_pct, total_net_profit, profit_factor, total_trades that scoring.py reads.
automation/tuner/scoring.py score() is IMPORTED (not reimplemented) and consumes the metrics dict; a result with relative_drawdown_pct > 15 scores strictly below one <= 15.
The engine returns a JSON-serializable result {metrics, score, params, meta} and can run in both tick mode and M5 bar (fast) mode.
All broker/metrics/engine unit tests pass on tiny synthetic fixtures with hand-computed expected values; no dependency on the 526MB CSV.
All new files pure ASCII; GaganEA.mq5 untouched; tools 16 + tuner 38 suites still green.
verification: python3 -m py_compile python_bt/broker.py python_bt/metrics.py python_bt/engine.py python_bt/scoring_bridge.py

python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'automation/tuner'); from scoring import score; print(score({'total_net_profit':100,'relative_drawdown_pct':10,'profit_factor':1.5,'total_trades':40}) > score({'total_net_profit':100,'relative_drawdown_pct':20,'profit_factor':1.5,'total_trades':40}))"  (expect True)
cd automation/tuner && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q  (expect 38 OK)
findings: Implemented python_bt/broker.py (Position + ClosedDeal dataclasses, Broker with hedging multi-position support, buy@ask/sell@bid fills, per-lot commission on open and each close, SL/TP crossing fills at the exact stop/target price, partial closes with proportional P&L, modify_sl, per-quote O(open_positions) equity + peak/trough drawdown trackers exposing max_drawdown_money, rel_drawdown_money/pct, absolute_drawdown). python_bt/metrics.py compute_metrics returns the exact analyzer-schema keys incl. relative_drawdown_pct; prefers broker drawdown trackers, falls back to equity-curve scan. Documented trade (round-trip, counted by trade_closed deals) vs deal (each partial/final close) in the module docstring; win/loss stats aggregate deals per position so a scaled-out position counts once. python_bt/scoring_bridge.py inserts automation/tuner on sys.path and re-exports score() (no reimplementation), consistent with tests/_bootstrap.py. python_bt/engine.py Engine drives a minimal strategy protocol (on_bar required, on_tick optional) via a Context (buy/sell/close_partial/close_full/modify_sl/positions/bid/ask/ts/bar); supports tick mode (tick-accurate, incremental M5 bar assembly so on_bar fires at bucket rollover) and bar (fast) mode (single closing quote per bar, approximation documented); returns JSON-serializable {metrics, score, params, meta} with inf profit_factor coerced to None for json.dumps while score() reads the live float. Tests: test_broker.py (fills, commission on open+close, buy TP/SL, sell SL/TP mirror, two partials + full close, over-volume partial -> full, hedging both directions, modify_sl breakeven, scripted peak-to-trough drawdown), test_metrics.py (3W/2L hand-computed PF/win_rate/expected_payoff/largest+avg, consecutive streaks, partials roll into one trade, zero-loss PF=inf, broker-tracker drawdown, empty ledger, score tier separation 10 vs 20), test_engine.py (always-buy stub tick+bar mode, JSON-serializable result).
